target_customer: Airlines and ferry operators; also defense customers (US Marine Corps contract, REGENT Defense from 2025)
problem: Regional coastal transport is slow and costly; electric aircraft range is short, so a ground-effect craft regulated as a maritime vessel could fly twice as far at lower cost.
business_model: Hardware sales of seaglider vessels to operators with pre-orders and deposits

founders.name: Mike Klinker
education: MIT, BS/MS aircraft controls and autonomy

technical_complexity.rationale: New vehicle class: full-scale electric flying boat with battery, hydrofoil and flight controls, plus maritime certification.

defensibility.rationale: Pre-orders, certification path and manufacturing are hard to copy; no patents examined.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it in sources; airlines and Lockheed Martin became investors or partners.

market_need_then: YC page claims >$10B in pre-orders and deposits from airlines and ferry companies four years in; company claims 180 mph and 180-mile range (not independently verified).

branding.brand_signature: Tagline 'Float. Foil. Fly.'; 'Seaglider' coined as product category name
branding.community_and_virality: Press on the company itself (Providence Journal, WCVB Chronicle) shown on own news page.

brand_strength.rationale: Own-site evidence only; the 'seaglider' category term is distinctive.

outcome_analysis: REGENT has progressed from a Winter 2021 YC pitch to a manufacturing facility (ribbon-cutting 2026-09-30), the first crewed seaglider flight (2026-09-02) and a $240M Series B headline (2026-08-27), per its own site. Strong founder-market fit (MIT, Aurora, Boeing) and strategic airline and defense backing explain the funding. The commercial outcome still depends on certification and delivery of the 12-seat model.
